senses.definition: (transitive) To bring into existence; (sometimes in particular:)
examples: You can create the color orange by mixing yellow and red.
… God created man a moral agent.

subsenses.definition: (especially of a god) To bring into existence out of nothing, without the prior existence of the materials or elements used.

quotes.text: In the beginning God created yᵉ heauen and the earth. And the earth was without forme & voyde, and darkenes was vpon the depe, & the Spirit of God moued vpon the waters.

subsenses.definition: To make or produce from other (e.g. raw, unrefined or scattered) materials or combinable elements or ideas; to design or invest with a new form, shape, function, etc.
examples: Couturiers create exclusive garments for an affluent clientele.

senses.definition: (transitive) To cause, to bring (a non-object) about by an action, behavior, or event, to occasion.
examples: crop failures created food shortages and high prices; his stubbornness created many difficulties
A sudden chemical spill on the highway created a chain‐collision which created a record traffic jam.

quotes.text: The turmoil went on—no rest, no peace. […] It was nearly eleven o'clock now, and he strolled out again. senses.definition: (transitive) To confer or invest with a rank or title of nobility, to appoint, ordain or constitute.
examples: Henry VIII created him a Duke. Last month, the queen created two barons.
Under the concordate with Belgium, at least one Belgian clergyman must be created cardinal; by tradition, every archbishop of Mechelen is thus created a cardinal.

senses.definition: (intransitive) To be or do something creative, imaginative, originative.
examples: Children usually enjoy creating, never mind if it is of any use!

senses.definition: (transitive) In theatre, to be the first performer of a role; to originate a character.
(UK, intransitive, colloquial) To make a fuss, complain; to shout.
